title: Ngô Dynasty
capsule: The Ngô dynasty was the first Vietnamese ruling house after nine centuries of Chinese domination, founded by Ngô Quyền following his decisive victory over the Southern Han fleet at the Battle of Bạch Đằng River in 938, where iron-tipped stakes planted in the riverbed destroyed the invading armada. Ngô Quyền established his capital at Cổ Loa and ruled as king until his death in 944; his brother-in-law Dương Tam Kha usurped power until 950, when two of Ngô Quyền's sons retook the throne as co-rulers. After the death of Ngô Xương Văn in 965, twelve regional warlords fragmented the country in what Vietnamese historiography calls the Anarchy of the Twelve Warlords, until Đinh Bộ Lĩnh reunified the realm and proclaimed the Đinh dynasty in 968. The Ngô period is foundational to Vietnamese national identity as the moment of restored independence.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Ngô dynasty's political history is attested in Vietnamese chronicles (Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư) and Chinese sources; the precise extent of territorial control during the anarchy period is uncertain, with many regions under autonomous warlords.
